q: What harmonic distortion limits should my factory meet at the supply point?
title: Harmonic distortion limits for a factory
short: BEE's MSME guidelines adopt IEEE 519-1992 limits at the point of common coupling: total voltage distortion of 8%, with 5% for any single harmonic, at 1 kV and below, and 5% total with 3% individual from 1 kV to 69 kV. Current limits depend on the ratio of short circuit current to load current.
audience: Electrical engineers and plant heads of factories with many drives, furnaces or UPS loads

ul: Bus voltage up to 1.0 kV: 5.0% individual harmonic, 8.0% total harmonic distortion (THD)
Above 1 kV up to 69 kV: 3.0% individual, 5.0% THD
Short circuit to load current ratio below 20: total demand distortion (TDD) 5.0%, with 4.0% for odd harmonics from the 3rd up to the 9th
Ratio from 20 to 50: TDD 8.0%, with 7.0% for odd harmonics from the 3rd up to the 9th
Higher harmonic orders have tighter limits in the same table

sections.h: Where and how often to measure
p: Measure at the point of common coupling, which BEE places between the plant and the supply network and between non-linear loads and other loads. Log voltage and current THD with a power analyser every month and check that filters are working.

ul: Pulse width modulation AC drives and drives with good choke filtering
Tuned LC filters, shunt filters or harmonic traps, and active filters
For new low voltage systems, transformers with built-in passive harmonic filtering

p: Your discom's supply code or connection agreement may set its own limits. Use those where they differ.

senseible: Senseible works from bills, so it sees the effect of harmonics only through units and power factor. Distortion itself needs a power analyser at the incomer.
